entities.name: Primary hyperfibrinolysis
observations: Paraneoplastic fibrinolytic bleeding syndrome reported with progressive prostate cancer; produces extensive hematomas, hypofibrinogenemia, elevated D-dimer, and preserved platelet count.
The presented values closely match a published 64-year-old prostate cancer case with thromboelastometric evidence of primary fibrinolysis and response to tranexamic acid plus cryoprecipitate.

entities.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
observations: Advanced prostate cancer can cause DIC with secondary hyperfibrinolysis, but classic consumption is less favored here because the platelet count is preserved and the reported case has a primary-fibrinolysis pattern.

entities.name: Acquired hemophilia A
observations: Typically causes isolated prolonged aPTT with normal PT and fibrinogen; requires mixing study, factor VIII activity, and inhibitor testing. This pattern does not fit simultaneous PT prolongation, hypofibrinogenemia, and elevated D-dimer.

entities.name: Prostate cancer
observations: Progressive malignant prostate disease is associated with rare paraneoplastic hyperfibrinolytic bleeding and can also cause DIC or acquired hemophilia.

entities.name: PMID:29320623
observations: Published case of a 64-year-old man with prostate cancer, extensive spontaneous hematomas, fibrinogen 1.068 g/L, D-dimer 1.122 mg/L, and primary hyperfibrinolysis; tranexamic acid and cryoprecipitate normalized findings.
